Re: Appeal of denial of total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I request a full reconsideration of the adverse benefit determination dated August 20, 2026, denying authorization for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472.

This appeal directly addresses the stated basis for denial: insufficient documentation of an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical record demonstrates that Morgan Mercado has completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate or durable relief:

- Symptoms have progressively worsened over 12 months despite rest.
- Morgan completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy from May 10, 2026, through July 5, 2026, including 16 visits focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening. The physical therapy discharge note documents this completed course.
- Morgan used NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection administered on May 11, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, Morgan continues to have severe pain and functional impairment, including inability to reach overhead, dress without assistance, or sleep on the affected side.

The objective findings support the need for surgery. June 8, 2026, shoulder radiographs showed complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirmed an intact rotator cuff. Examination demonstrated glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with intact cuff strength. These findings are consistent with advanced structural joint disease and substantial loss of function after failed nonsurgical treatment.

The record also documents the absence of identified contraindicating concerns: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, Morgan is a nonsmoker, and BMI is 29. The requested procedure is being recommended by Lindqvist, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

Accordingly, the record addresses the conservative-treatment issue identified in the denial. Please reverse the denial and authorize CPT 23472.

If Highmark continues to rely on criteria not included in the denial notice, please provide the complete medical policy, utilization criteria, clinical guideline, or other review criteria actually applied to this request, including its title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific provisions used in reaching the determination. I have not been provided the governing policy text, so this appeal does not quote or assume any policy language.

Please also provide the clinical rationale for any continued denial and identify any additional documentation required. If the plan determines that a peer-to-peer discussion or expedited review is appropriate, please arrange it promptly with Lindqvist, MD.

Enclosed are or will be submitted with this appeal:

1. The August 20, 2026, denial notice;
2. The physical therapy records and discharge note documenting 16 visits from May 10 through July 5, 2026;
3. Medication history documenting four months of NSAID treatment;
4. Records of the May 11, 2026, corticosteroid injection and its three-week partial response;
5. June 8, 2026, shoulder radiographs;
6. CT report confirming an intact rotator cuff;
7. Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Lindqvist, MD; and
8. Relevant clinical records documenting the absence of active infection and other reported risk factors.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me of the appeal tracking number and review timeline. The appeal must be received by February 16, 2027, based on the deadline stated in the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Morgan Mercado
